widget_map.conflicts: TOTALS RULE: the concept adds a 'Coaching' column and includes it in Total. The current code deliberately excludes it, with the comment 'Total the displayed crew-routine columns only; manager coaching sessions have no column here'. Coaching sessions are generated by org admins, not crew, so adding them inflates 'crew engagement'. Recommend a visually separated Coaching column excluded from Total, or no column; this needs a decision. Naming: 'Sim' versus ROUTINE_LABELS 'Simulator session', and column order Flight/Sim/Training/Debrief versus the current Sim/Flight/Debrief/Training. A team filter on small teams (for example 'Cabin', 4 members) can expose individuals' activity; enforce k >= 5.
widget_map.implementation_notes: TableWidget at preset XL 8x4. Week cell = w.week.split('-')[1] ('W41'). Total in <strong>, numbers tabular-nums. Footer `Last ${weeks} weeks · total ${grand}`. Tools: 'Export CSV' -> /api/admin/export/weekly.csv?weeks=. 'Filter' -> popover for routine type (team only with suppression). widget_map.widget: consents: 'Sharing requests' (list, Dashboard, c4 x 3). Pending 6 / Approved 38 / Declined 4 / Expired 11
widget_map.current_equivalent: src/app/admin/page.tsx: SideCard 'Sharing requests' using RuleList, with Pending (dot warn), Approved (ok), Declined (bad), Expired (neutral).
widget_map.data_source: org_engagement_stats() -> 'consents' = status -> count(*) from public.consent_requests where organization_id = v_org, over all time. consent_requests RLS consent_select allows requester, target or super admin only, so org admins cannot read rows; that is correct.
widget_map.full_view: /admin/engagement/sharing, aggregates only. It shows requests per ISO week by status and by routine_type (simulator / flight / debrief / training), approval rate, median time to respond (responded_at - requested_at), approvals still valid (valid_until > now()) versus lapsed, and expiry rate. No names and no pairs.
widget_map.gaps: The counts have no time window. 'approved' includes approvals whose valid_until has passed, because the status stays 'approved'. Stale pending rows become 'expired' only via pg_cron private.expire_consents() (hourly) or expire_stale_consents(), so where pg_cron is unavailable Pending overstates. There is no RPC for the breakdowns; add org_consent_stats(p_weeks) that computes the effective status (pending with expires_at < now() counts as expired).
widget_map.conflicts: BLIND SYNERGY: 'Review' and 'Remind' imply acting on individual requests. Consent is strictly between two crew members: consent_insert pins the requester, and consent_update_target lets only the target resolve. Showing an org admin who asked whom, or letting the admin nudge a target to approve, breaks consent-gated Blind Synergy and introduces coercion. Do not build per-request review or remind. Re-scope 'Review' to the aggregate full view, and drop 'Remind' (or make it an org-wide, identity-free reminder that pending requests exist). Colours: the concept has Pending red and Declined grey; current has Pending warn and Declined bad.
widget_map.implementation_notes: ListWidget with 4 rows, the last row bottom-aligned with no divider. Tool 'Review' -> /admin/engagement/sharing. Remove 'Remind', or replace it with a disabled tool whose tooltip explains why.

new_capabilities: PER-USER CANVAS LAYOUT PERSISTENCE. New table public.dashboard_layouts. Columns: user_id uuid not null references public.users(id) on delete cascade; surface text not null check in ('crew','org_admin','super_admin'); page text not null check (page ~ '^[a-z_]{2,32}$') with values such as 'overview', 'users', 'ingest', 'coaching' and 'rewards'; schema_version int not null default 1; items jsonb not null default '[]' check (jsonb_typeof(items) = 'array' and pg_column_size(items) < 16384); locked boolean not null default false; updated_at timestamptz not null default now(); primary key (user_id, surface, page). Each item is {id: widgetId, size: 'S'|'M'|'L'|'XL' or {w, h}, order int, x?: int, y?: int, pinned: bool, hidden: bool, snoozed_until?: timestamptz}. RLS: enable it, with select, insert, update and delete for authenticated using (user_id = (select auth.uid())). WITH CHECK adds that user_id = auth.uid(), that the org_admin surface requires private.current_user_role() in ('org_admin','super_admin'), and that the super_admin surface requires private.is_super_admin(). Grants follow the lockdown memory: revoke all from anon and authenticated, then grant select, insert, update and delete to authenticated explicitly. Write path: server action saveCanvasLayout(surface, page, items, expectedUpdatedAt) in src/lib/canvas/actions.ts. It validates items with Zod against the registry (unknown ids dropped, sizes restricted to each widget's allowedSizes), uses optimistic concurrency on updated_at so two open tabs don't silently overwrite each other, and debounces from the client. Read: one select per page render; the code default applies when no row exists. Add negative cases to scripts/rls-check.mjs (reading or writing another user's layout) and regenerate types with npm run db:types.

OPTIONAL ORG DEFAULT LAYOUT. Table public.org_dashboard_defaults (organization_id uuid references organizations on delete cascade, surface text, page text, items jsonb, updated_by uuid, updated_at; primary key (organization_id, surface, page)). RLS: select where organization_id = private.current_org_id(); insert and update where private.is_org_admin_of(organization_id). This would let an org admin set the crew canvas default for their org. It is a product decision; without it, defaults live in code at src/lib/canvas/defaults.ts.

WIDGET REGISTRY AND LIBRARY ('Add'). This is code, not a table: src/lib/canvas/registry.ts, mapping widgetId -> {title, surface, page, roles, allowedSizes: {S|M|L|XL: [w, h]}, defaultSize, headerMeta(data), tools: [{label, icon, primary, kind: 'link'|'action'|'client', href|action, needsRowSelection}], fullViewHref, loader}. The library sheet lists that page's widgets which are hidden or not yet placed; adding one appends to items. Size presets: the crew boards define S 3x2, M 4x3, L 5x3, XL 8x4, with per-widget variants on the sizes board ('S · 4×2', 'M · 7×3', 'M · 5×3'). The org admin board also uses 4x4, 8x5, 4x2, 7x5, 5x2, 7x4 and 5x4, so presets must be defined per widget. Text never shrinks; smaller sizes show fewer rows.

PIN, HIDE, LOCK, ARRANGE, RESET, RESIZE SEMANTICS (from the crew guide copy). 'Pin': 'Keep it in place when you auto-arrange'; stored as items[].pinned. 'Resize': 'Change its span on the grid'; items[].size, restricted to allowedSizes. 'Hide': 'Remove it from the canvas (not from the app)'; items[].hidden, and 'Add' brings it back. 'Lock': 'Freeze the layout so nothing moves by accident'; dashboard_layouts.locked, which disables drag, resize, hide and arrange. 'Arrange': 'Pack widgets onto the grid without gaps'; client-side dense packing over unpinned items, which fixes the empty columns beside 'How mapping works', 'Invite a member' and 'Add a reward'. 'Reset': 'Back to the default layout'; deletes the row. Every action must also have a keyboard path (see risks). All of these persist through saveCanvasLayout.

DRAG AND RESIZE ON A 12-COLUMN SNAP GRID. Pointer drag by the title bar, with a dashed free-slot placeholder ('Drop a widget into the dashed free slot' in the crew guide). Breakpoints: 12 columns, 6 at 1180px and below, 1 at 720px and below. Every span class must be remapped at each breakpoint, including c8, which the prototype forgets. Implement in-house or with a bundled library; nothing loads from a CDN because the CSP is script-src 'self'.

SELECTION MODEL AND CONTEXT BAR. A client CanvasProvider with selectedWidgetId, plus selectedRowIds for table widgets ('Approve', 'Deliver', 'Cancel', 'Assign team', 'Edit', 'Deactivate' and 'Open' act on rows). Deselect via the 'Esc' tool, the Escape key (ignored while a Modal or Drawer is open) and clicking empty canvas. Selection is client-only and not persisted.

SNOOZE. It is not on the org admin board, but the crew board defines 'Snooze': 'Hide it until next week.' If it is ever needed for attention widgets (Missing reports, Redemption requests), store it as items[].snoozed_until in dashboard_layouts rather than in a separate table. The server filters snoozed items when rendering.

GUIDE PROGRESS. New table public.guide_progress (user_id uuid references users on delete cascade; guide_id text check (guide_id ~ '^[a-z0-9_.-]{2,64}$'), e.g. 'org_admin_canvas_v1'; step int not null default 0 check (step between 0 and 49); completed_at timestamptz; dismissed_at timestamptz; updated_at timestamptz default now(); primary key (user_id, guide_id)). RLS: own rows only for select, insert and update; grants explicit. Route: server action saveGuideProgress. No org admin guide steps exist in the concept, so they must be authored; the data-guide anchors (members, reports, avgcredits, reflections, weekly, tiers, consents, needs, privacy, userstable, teams, missing, invite, profiles, batch, ingestnote, coachform, coachhow, coachlog, requests, catalog, addreward, ctxbar, mainbar) already exist. The guide reopens from the main bar, and the card follows the CSS rule: 'never lower than 20px above the main bar'.

SEARCH / COMMAND PALETTE (main-bar 'Search'). No new table. Route: server action searchAdmin(q), or GET /api/admin/search?q=, with q sanitised the same way as users/page.tsx (/[^\p{L}\p{N} @._-]/gu, maximum 80 characters). It returns: members (users in the org by full_name or email ilike, under RLS users_select); rewards and redemptions (RLS); tokens (admin_wall_list_profiles filtered by code prefix, service role after assertRole); and pages and widgets from the registry (select or scroll to a widget). Org-scoped and lightly rate-limited (admin_check_rate_limit key search:user:<id>).

THEME. The main-bar 'Theme' button reuses useTheme (cookie 'theme', data-theme on html). The concept defines no dark tokens: navy #0E153E, red #BD2025, hue 275. Add light tokens (--ink navy, --brand red, --brandsoft, --line, --line2, --soft track) and derive dark equivalents in src/app/globals.css under [data-theme='dark']. Keep red-for-CTA separate from the --bad danger token.

risks: Anonymity wall and Blind Synergy. 'Review' and 'Remind' on Sharing requests would expose who asked whom and pressure targets. Exclude them; aggregate full view only.

Small-cell re-identification. Any team or category 'Filter' on Weekly activity, Training-needs, Tiers or Avg. credits can single out individuals in small groups ('Cabin' has 4 members). Enforce k >= 5 suppression server-side in the RPCs, never in the client.

Exports. Members and redemptions CSVs carry PII, and the current toCsv has no formula-injection guard. Coaching guidance and reflection text must never be exportable. Every export needs audit({critical: true}), rate limiting and cache-control no-store.

Privilege escalation. The 'Role: Org admin' option in 'Invite a member' lets org admins mint admins, which no path allows today (only createOrgAdmin under /super). It needs an explicit policy and RLS WITH CHECK.

Copy accuracy. The 'Anonymity wall' sentence ('Everything on this dashboard is an aggregate… no individual outputs') is false on the Users, Coaching and Rewards canvases. Keep it Dashboard-only, or users will be misled about what admins can see.

Semantic drift. 'Coaching' (an org-admin routine) is counted into crew weekly totals and shown among crew routines on the sibling crew boards. The current product rule keeps it manager-only and excluded from totals; mixing them corrupts engagement metrics and suggests crew can run coaching.

Naming inconsistency across concept boards. Tiers are 'Ready → Proficient' on the crew boards, Bronze/Silver/Gold/Platinum on the admin boards, and the DB has thresholds 0/100/300/600 versus the super board's 0/150/500/1,200. Tokens are 'SKY-…' versus the DB constraint '^PROF-[0-9]{4}[A-Z]-[A-Z]$'. Role and category values don't match the users.role and operational_category enums. Brand 'S3' versus 'Cognitive Copilot'. 'Org admin' versus ROLE_LABELS 'Organization admin'.

Colour semantics. Brand red #BD2025 is used both for primary CTAs and for attention states ('Missing', 'Pending', 'Requested', the Gold tier). With no separate danger token, users can't tell 'act here' from 'something is wrong'. Approved and Delivered tones also change meaning.

Accessibility of drag and resize. WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7 (Dragging Movements) and 2.1.1 (Keyboard) need non-drag alternatives: Move up / Move down / Move to slot and Resize S/M/L/XL as buttons in the context bar, roving tabindex across widgets, and arrow keys while in 'move mode'. Also needed: aria-live announcements for 'Widget selected: …', moves and size changes, and focus return after Hide and Reset.

Title bar as a button. The concept nests the widget title, which should be a heading, inside a full-width <button>. Headings are not allowed inside a button, and screen readers lose the document outline. Use a heading plus a separate select control, or role=group with an aria-label.

Keyboard. The prototype has no Escape handler and no visible focus styles, and its hover styles are dead because inline backgrounds win. Escape for deselect must not conflict with the Escape handling of Modal and Drawer (useOverlay) or with native select dropdowns. Tab order across the left bar, the canvas and the bottom bar must be logical, and a skip link to the canvas is needed.

Small text. Tool labels at 10px/700, badges at 10px and the 'ORG ADMIN' label at 11px fall below comfortable reading size. The toolbar unit clamp(10px, 0.9vw, 13px) shrinks to 10px around 1110px wide.

Prototype CSS defects not to copy. .mainbar>button.main forces a 4.9em width onto the text tabs (the labels overlap, as in the page5 screenshot), the badge override squashes badges to 16x8, and c8 is not remapped at <=1180px and <=720px (implicit columns and horizontal overflow). The context title also breaks as 'Nothing selecte / d'.

Phones. The org admin board has no phone design. At 375px the sticky main bar (logo, 5 tabs, 4 tools, 2 links, account) wraps to several rows and eats the viewport, and the context bar strip pushes content down. Tables inside narrow widgets need column hiding (the current code uses max-md:hidden). Inputs must stay at 16px on phones to avoid iOS zoom; the .ctl rule exists, but the concept uses 15px. Adopt the crew phone pattern (action sheet for the selected widget, condensed tab bar) and disable drag on touch in favour of explicit Move buttons.

Server data fan-out and performance. Each canvas page renders every widget server-side. Users already runs two queries, one of up to 2000 rows; Ingestion calls admin_wall_list_profiles, which returns every profile; adding Teams, Missing, layouts and badges adds more. The admin layout would add a service-role wall RPC to every navigation. Use one aggregate RPC per page, pagination, Suspense boundaries per widget, and avoid re-rendering every widget on a selection change (context state confined to the chrome).

Layout persistence. Saves from two tabs (last write wins), stale widget ids after renames, or invalid spans after breakpoint changes can corrupt layouts. Version the items, validate against the registry, use optimistic concurrency on updated_at, and fall back to defaults on parse failure.

CSP (next.config.ts). script-src is 'self' 'unsafe-inline' and font-src is 'self' data:, so drag libraries, icons, fonts and the S3 logo must be bundled locally, never loaded from a CDN. Grid placement through inline style attributes depends on style-src 'unsafe-inline'; if CSP is ever tightened to nonces or hashes, move spans to classes or CSS variables set from classes. Manrope already comes from next/font (self-hosted) with weights 400 to 800, latin only; the concept also ships cyrillic, greek and vietnamese subsets.

Upload limits. The concept hard-codes '10 MB each', but MAX_PDF_MB is 4 on Netlify (limits.ts). Bulk CSV import cannot go through server actions (bodySizeLimit '1mb'). Netlify's 60 s function cap is why uploads stay one file per request.

Email infrastructure. Invitations ('Invites expire in 7 days') and reminders assume email delivery, but the repo has no SMTP or provider and the demo deployments have none. Without a copy-link fallback, onboarding breaks.

Eligibility leaks. If coaching candidates show why someone is ineligible ('opted out' versus 'no report'), the admin learns a privacy choice. Return only eligible true or false. Note that runCoachingRoutine's error 'This employee has disabled sharing' already leaks the reason and should be generalised.

Super admins on /admin have no organizationId. Every widget, export and RPC must handle the missing-org case (today it is a Banner per page). Actions use resolveOrgScope and require an explicit organization_id for super admins, so either add an org picker or keep the read-only empty states.
